Phase A: Foundations (Weeks 1–4) - Endurance work: 2–3 days/week of cardio, transitioning to longer and steadier efforts in Week 3–4; Approach: walk/run intervals as tolerated (e.g., 2 minutes walk, 1 minute jog, repeat).
Phase B: Build running tolerance and rhythm (Weeks 5–8) - Run-walk templates: e.g., 3 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk; progress to 4 minutes jog / 1 minute walk as tolerated.
Weekly long-session progression: increase a single longer cardio session by 5–10 minutes every week if well tolerated, up to ~35–45 minutes of total continuous or near-continuous effort by Week 8.
Optional: introduce a very light, controlled continuous jog of 10–15 minutes once per week if he reports comfort and no symptoms.
Phase C: 5K readiness and taper prep (Weeks 9–12) - Structure: 1 dedicated cardio session that is a near-5K effort, but not all-out, using a run-walk approach.

Week 9–10: target approximately 25–30 minutes of continuous-like effort (run-walk) with a moderate pace; include a practice 5K trial in a controlled environment if medical clearance and comfort allow.
Week 11: testing window opens. If not ready, perform another shorter test (e.g., 2–3 miles or time-limited run-walk) rather than a full 5K.

Week 12: Optional formal 5K time trial, if he achieved a consistent, symptom-free conditioning base and cardiologist approves. If not ready, schedule a re-test after a few more weeks of progressive endurance work.

Run-walk and pacing guidelines: Start conservative (e.g., 1 minute jog / 2 minutes walk) for the first 10–15 minutes; increase jogging time as tolerated while maintaining ability to talk; use steady, controlled pace; avoid sprinting.

Safety protocol during the test: Have a supportive training partner or staff member present; keep a portable HR monitor but rely primarily on RPE and ability to speak; stop immediately if warning signs appear and seek medical evaluation.

Possible next deliverables: a detailed week-by-week plan with explicit run-walk templates and weekly cardio minutes; a test protocol document for medical team; a backup field-test or submaximal assessment plan.
If you’d like, a precise 12-week progression with weekly cardio templates tailored to run-walk intervals can be drafted, plus a Week-12 readiness test plan.

raw_text:
Here is a cohesive, 12-week plan summary that blends all the previous elements: cardio emphasis for weight loss, expanded strength work with safe compound lifts (goblet squats and Romanian deadlifts), maintained safety for a 58-year-old male six months post-MI cleared for moderate-intensity exercise. The plan uses four resistance days per week (two upper, two lower) and four cardio days, with optional active recovery. It integrates progression, safety cues, and practical substitutions for equipment.

Overall structure
- Frequency: 4 resistance sessions per week (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B) + 4 cardio sessions (Cardio A: steady-state, Cardio B: intervals/tempo, Cardio C: longer easy, Cardio D: optional HIIT in Phase 3 if approved). Optional 5th day for mobility/recuperation.
- Phases:
  - Phase 1: Foundation and technique (Weeks 1–4)
  - Phase 2: Progressive overload with cardio emphasis (Weeks 5–8)
  - Phase 3: Conditioning, fat loss focus, and integration of HIIT option (Weeks 9–12)
- Compounds added: Goblet squats and Romanian deadlifts (RDLs) integrated on lower-body days with safe progressions. Substitutions available (leg press, hip thrusts, split squats, trap-bar deadlifts).

Weekly template (typical week)
- Mon: Cardio A (endurance) + Optional core
- Tue: Upper-Body Strength A
- Wed: Cardio B (intervals/tempo)
- Thu: Lower-Body Strength A (with Goblet Squats and RDLs)
- Fri: Upper-Body Strength B
- Sat: Cardio C/D (longer easy or optional HIIT in Phase 3)
- Sun: Lower-Body Strength B (and/or mobility) or rest

Key safety guardrails (reiterated)
- HR targets: under 115 bpm for most sessions; use RPE and talk test as practical guides, especially with medications like beta-blockers.
- No max lifts; control tempo; avoid Valsalva; exhale on exertion.
- Rest: 60–90 seconds between most sets; 2–3 minutes after heavy compounds if needed.
- Symptoms: chest pain, dizziness, severe shortness of breath require stopping and medical check.

Phase-by-phase details (summary with specifics)

Phase 1: Foundations (Weeks 1–4)
- Goals: establish routine, technique, and confidence in both aerobic and resistance work.
- Cardio progression:
  - Cardio A: 25–40 minutes total at a comfortable pace (HR ~95–105 bpm; or RPE 4–5).
  - Cardio B: 20–25 minutes with light intervals initially (e.g., 1 min work at RPE 5–6, 2 min easy; total ~4–6 intervals).
  - Optional Cardio C: 15–25 minutes easy on non-lifting days.
- Resistance: 2–3 sets x 8–12 reps per exercise; emphasis on technique, tempo 3–0–2 or similar.
  - Upper A: Seated chest press, Seated row, Lat pulldown or assisted pull-down, Seated shoulder press, Cable triceps pushdown, Dumbbell biceps curl; core stability.
  - Lower A: Goblet squats (2–3 x 8–12), Romanian deadlifts with light dumbbells (2–3 x 8–12), Leg press or leg extension, Leg curl, Hip bridge, Standing calf raise; core.
- Phase 1 progression: maintain form; move to 3 sets on many exercises by Week 3–4 if technique is solid.

Phase 2: Progressive overload + cardio emphasis (Weeks 5–8)
- Cardio: increase duration and introduce more robust intervals.
  - Cardio A: 35–45 minutes steady-state at brisk pace (RPE 5–6).
  - Cardio B: 6–8 intervals of 1:30–2:00 work with 1:30–2:00 rest; or 2–3 blocks of 2-minute tempo segments.
  - Cardio C: 25–40 minutes easy to moderate as needed.
- Resistance: 3 sets x 8–12 reps for most exercises; add light supersets only if form remains pristine and HR safety is ensured.
  - Lower B: Goblet squats, RDLs, Hip hinge variations, Leg curl, Leg extension, Split squats or step-ups, Hip ab/adduction, Calf raises.
  - Upper B: Incline press or incline dumbbell press, Seated/cable row variation, Assisted pull-down, Lateral raises, Overhead triceps extension, Dumbbell curls.
- Progressions: 5–10% load increases when form is solid; time-under-tension emphasis via slower tempo for lower body.
- Core and mobility: 8–12 minutes post-workout; emphasis on anti-rotation.

Phase 3: Conditioning, consolidation, and HIIT integration (Weeks 9–12)
- Cardio: higher total volume; begin HIIT cautiously if medically cleared.
  - Cardio A: 45–60 minutes steady-state (1 longer session per week), with 5–10 minute tempo blocks as tolerated.
  - Cardio B: HIIT integration if approved: start with 6–8 intervals of 20–30 seconds work at RPE 5–6 with 90–120 seconds rest; or 1–2 cycles of 1–2 minutes work with 2–3 minutes rest.
  - Cardio C: Longer easy session; optional as needed to reach caloric targets.
- Resistance: 3–4 sets x 6–10 reps for major lifts in Weeks 9–10; Weeks 11–12 maintain 6–10 reps or 8–12 with emphasis on form; reduce if symptoms arise.
  - Lower: Goblet squats continue as primary squat, RDLs continue as posterior chain hinge; add light trap-bar deadlifts if safe; split squats as progression.
  - Upper: Compound pressing and pulling movements with machines or dumbbells; continue progressions with caution.
- HIIT guidance (Phase 3): only after cardiologist confirmation; start with 1 HIIT session every 1–2 weeks; monitor HR with RPE; adjust frequency based on recovery.

Compound lifts specifics (integration details)
- Goblet Squats: start 2–3 sets x 8–12 reps with 8–12 kg dumbbell or kettlebell; tempo 3–0–2; progression: +2–4 kg when form is solid for two consecutive workouts.
- Romanian Deadlifts: start 2–3 sets x 8–12 reps with light dumbbells or trap bar; tempo 3–1–2; progression: small weight increase when back and hamstring tolerance is good.
- Substitutions: Leg press, hip thrusts, split squats, box squats as needed for safety or equipment access.

Example week (illustrative)
- Week 6 (mid-Phase 2 example):
  - Monday: Cardio A 40 minutes; Core
  - Tuesday: Upper A (3 sets x 8–12)
  - Wednesday: Cardio B intervals 6 x 1:30 with 1:30 rest
  - Thursday: Lower A including Goblet Squats 3 x 8–12 and RDLs 3 x 8–12
  - Friday: Upper B (3 sets x 8–12)
  - Saturday: Cardio C 25–35 minutes easy
  - Sunday: Lower B (3 sets x 8–12)

Nutrition alignment (short recap)
- Protein: 1.0–1.2 g/kg/day; distribute across meals; post-workout protein 20–40 g.
- Carbs: around workouts; higher on cardio days; moderate on rest days.
- Fats: 25–35% of calories, focus on unsaturated fats; omega-3s through fish or supplements per clinician advice.
- Sodium: align with cardiologist guidance; typically 1500–2300 mg/day.
- Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day plus adjustments for exercise.

Monitoring and safety
- Weekly check-ins on symptoms, energy, sleep, and weight.
- Use HR as a supplementary guide; rely on RPE and talk test for lifts, especially with meds.
- If any red flags appear (chest pain, dizziness, near-syncope, unusual fatigue), pause and consult clinician.

Deliverables I can provide next
- A precise, week-by-week, day-by-day 12-week plan with exact exercise names, sets, reps, tempo, rest intervals for all resistance and cardio days.
- A printable client handout summarizing the plan, including the two compound movements with cues, safety reminders, and progression pathways.
- A run-walk 5K readiness plan if you want to maintain the current 5K testing objective, aligned with the new strength emphasis.
